hypotheses.reasoning: notification-svc heap climbs steadily from about 20:44 onward while GC pauses look normal. At #1719 (20:49:18) a full GC leaves old gen unreclaimed at 78%, and #2171 shows 87% with 35% GC overhead. This looks like an unbounded messageCache leak. The heap then exhausts: OutOfMemoryError at messageCache.put (#2250), and pods are OOMKilled at the 2Gi limit (#2253, #2482, #2647). Each kill drops the service, and api-gateway returns 502 'connection reset (no healthy upstream)' on POST /v1/notify (#2362, #2411, #2656, #3098). Those gateway 502s are downstream symptoms and are not cited as origin. Alternatives ruled out: the 401s from catalog-svc translation API and the search 502s sit on a separate path (search-api/web-bff), not notify; legacy-inventory healthcheck timeouts are status-poller noise; template-svc is healthy with 0 errors.

The slow template-svc render (#1118, 2975ms) could have increased in-flight work and memory in notification-svc and amplified the leak. Weak evidence: template-svc logged no errors and its renders are mostly fast (about 30-90ms), so this is not the primary cause.

verdict.recommendedAction: Restarting is only temporary mitigation. Capture a heap dump from notification-svc, find what retains entries in messageCache (missing eviction or TTL, or unbounded growth), and ship a fix that bounds the cache. Add a heap-usage alert on notification-svc. Short term, consider raising the memory limit or adding replicas to reduce the impact of restarts on the notify path.

hypotheses.reasoning: notification-svc heap climbs steadily from about 20:44 onward while GC pauses look normal. At #1719 (20:49:18) a full GC leaves old gen unreclaimed at 78%, and #2171 shows 87% with 35% GC overhead. This looks like an unbounded messageCache leak. The heap then exhausts: OutOfMemoryError at messageCache.put (#2250), and pods are OOMKilled at the 2Gi limit (#2253, #2482, #2647). Each kill drops the service, and api-gateway returns 502 'connection reset (no healthy upstream)' on POST /v1/notify (#2362, #2411, #2656, #3098). Those gateway 502s are downstream symptoms and are not cited as origin. Alternatives ruled out: the 401s from catalog-svc translation API and the search 502s sit on a separate path (search-api/web-bff), not notify; legacy-inventory healthcheck timeouts are status-poller noise; template-svc is healthy with 0 errors.

The slow template-svc render (#1118, 2975ms) could have increased in-flight work and memory in notification-svc and amplified the leak. Weak evidence: template-svc logged no errors and its renders are mostly fast (about 30-90ms), so this is not the primary cause.
